state:
Goal `core-objectmap`. `Core\ObjectMap` has its class card, and `clear`, `count`, `get`, `has`, `isEmpty` and `set` have every feature proof: about, examples, attack, bench with a recorded figure, and a Novis and a Rust test each.
`has` and `isEmpty` record 0 allocations. `set` records 1 allocation of 50 bytes per overwrite: the value store is written through `NvsArray::set`, which takes an owned `NvsStr` key, so an overwrite builds the chain key on the heap even though the entry already exists (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:382`). The bench declares no allocation count; the Backlog carries the fix.
`bun nv proofs --owed --group 'Core\ObjectMap'` names what is left: `remove` (examples, hostile, perf), `keys` and `values` (examples, hostile, perf, and a Novis test each).

items.text: **`Core\ObjectMap::remove`** — owes examples, hostile, perf (check `about` with `--id`). Its Rust test is `the_two_stores_stay_paired_through_set_and_remove`, and `tests/conformance/core/object-map-get-and-remove-on-an-absent-key.nvst` calls it. A bench that removes and re-adds one key will allocate on the re-add; measure a remove of an absent key for `allocations 0`, or declare none. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:434`

**`Core\ObjectMap::keys`** — owes examples, hostile, perf and a Novis test: add `// covers: Core\ObjectMap::keys` to `tests/conformance/core/object-map-keys-on-identity.nvst`. It returns a new list, so its bench allocates. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:476`
**`Core\ObjectMap::values`** — the same as `keys`, and the same case can carry both markers. `rule:testing/feature-proofs`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/objmap.rs:486`

backlog: `Core\ObjectMap::set` allocates its chain key on every overwrite. A borrowed-key replace on `NvsArray` (beside `NvsArray::set`, `crates/nvs-runtime/src/array.rs:953`) would take it to 0; then add `// bench: allocations 0` to `benches/members/core/ObjectMap/set.nvs` and re-record. `Core\ObjectSet` may share the cost. Owner: this goal, after the member proofs.
